surprises.description: JCI guided FY27 organic growth to 11%–12%, above the preview’s 9%–10% base expectation and the 9%–10% consensus framework. The guide’s $6.15–$6.30 adjusted EPS range is also modestly above the $6.13 consensus at its midpoint.
surprises.fact_evidence: “FY27 guidance calls for organic revenue growth of 11% to 12%” and “adjusted EPS of $6.15 to $6.30.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “FY27 … consensus is $6.13 (+20.7%)”; the base scenario expected “$6.10–6.20, organic +9–10%.”

surprises.description: Q4 organic revenue growth was 12%, exceeding the preview’s 9%–10% expectation and even the bull scenario’s 11%+ threshold.
surprises.expectation_evidence: Q4 company guidance was “organic +9–10%”; the bull scenario called for “organic +11%+.”

surprises.description: Q4 orders accelerated sharply to 44%, rather than continuing the deceleration the preview highlighted from 39% to 30% to 27%. They also substantially exceeded the preview’s 20% threshold for a bullish result.
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview highlighted orders “decelerating (39→30→27%)” and said the bull case required Q4 orders to “hold ≥20% organic.”

surprises.description: Backlog reached a record $23 billion, above the preview’s base expectation of $21.5–$22.0 billion and the bullish scenario’s $23 billion-plus mark. The reported $2 billion increase from the preview’s $21.0 billion Q3 level also exceeded the base sequential build implied there.
surprises.expectation_evidence: The base scenario expected backlog of “$21.5–22.0B”; the bull scenario said “$23B+.”

surprises.description: FY26 adjusted free-cash-flow conversion reached 103%, slightly above the preview’s approximately 100% expectation and exceeding the company’s prior guidance.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Adjusted free cash flow conversion reached 103% ($3.2 billion), all exceeding prior guidance.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview listed FY26 adjusted FCF conversion at “~100%.”

surprises.description: FY26 adjusted EPS growth was 37%, modestly ahead of the preview’s 35.1% consensus growth expectation and above the company’s prior guidance.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Adjusted EPS grew 37%” for FY26, “exceeding prior guidance.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview showed FY26 adjusted EPS consensus growth of “+35.1%” and company guidance of “~$5.05.”

surprises.description: JCI announced a new restructuring program with approximately $400 million of FY27–FY28 expense to generate about $600 million in annualized savings by FY29. The preview mentioned possible portfolio actions but did not anticipate this specific program or its cost-and-savings targets.
surprises.fact_evidence: “A new restructuring program targets approximately $400 million in expense over FY27-FY28 to deliver about $600 million in gross annualized savings by FY29.”

surprises.description: The prior restructuring program generated run-rate savings $100 million to $150 million above its original $500 million target, a favorable outcome not discussed in the preview.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The prior restructuring program delivered run-rate savings $100 million to $150 million above its original $500 million target.”

surprises.description: JCI disclosed that its pending sale of the global intrusion business is expected to close around Q2 FY27 and carry about $0.15 of annualized EPS dilution. The preview discussed a prior HVAC divestiture and possible portfolio actions, but did not flag this transaction or its dilution.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The pending divestiture of the ~$500 million-revenue global intrusion (residential/light commercial) business is expected to close around Q2 FY27 and be dilutive by about $0.15 annualized.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview’s catalyst checklist included “any portfolio action,” but did not identify this divestiture or quantify dilution.

surprises.description: Management said the Armada partnership’s 500 MW target has higher TAM per megawatt than typical data-center work. The preview already cited the 500 MW target, but did not flag this higher-TAM characterization.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The Armada partnership targets 500 megawatts of distributed edge compute capacity in 2027 at a higher TAM per megawatt than typical data center work.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview described “Armada … to deploy 500 MW” by 2027.
